newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI index up 5 pct as foreigners return.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI index up 5 pct as foreigners return.

text.p: Slovenian shares surged over five percent in early trade on Tuesday and traders attributed the rally to resurgent foreign buying, adding shares could gain another eight percent this week.

"This is crazy because foreigners are buying everything. Apparently they decided to resume investing in Slovenia after mulling it for the past four months," said Milos Pelcar, a trader of bank A banka.
By 0935 GMT the blue-chip SBI index was up 5.65 percent at 1,333.81.
Traders said foreigners were especially targetting petrol trader Petrol and drug companies Lek and Krka.
By 0930 GMT Petrol, the most actively traded share, was up 7.84 percent to 18,980 tolars, while Lek firmed 6.59 percent to 26,700. Krka rose 12.7 percent to 19,500.
Traders said foreign buying was executed almost entirely by the Slovenian branch of Austria's Creditanstalt. Nobody at the bank was immediately available for comment.

Foreign investors stopped buying Slovenian shares in February when the Bank of Slovenia said they had to open fiduciary accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in securities. Since then the index had lost 20 percent.

The banks estimated the cost of the accounts at an average of 12 percent of the amount handled due to an expansive balancing between the money paid into the accounts that would have to be considered as liabilities that needed to be balanced by the bank's foreign exchange assets.
Last week the central bank decided to ease the rules by saying that the balancing was not necessary in cases when foreign investors buy shares for a minimum period of seven years.

"Although seven years is a long time, foreigners believe the central bank would have to ease rules earlier than that in line with Slovenia's association membership in the European Union -- which is expected to be enforced next year," an analyst said.
